## Current work

**Immune control of heart regeneration.** Newborn mammalian hearts can regenerate
after injury; adult hearts cannot. My work shows that the PD-1/PD-L1 checkpoint
pathway maintains the immunosuppressive environment this regenerative window
depends on, and asks how T cell populations are recruited and licensed during
neonatal cardiac injury.

**Self-renewal and ageing of tissue-resident macrophages.** During my PhD I
characterised a short isoform of Piwil2 required for the self-renewal of murine
macrophages, and contributed to work on how alveolar macrophages retain their
epigenetic identity through long-term expansion and how microglia mature in the
developing brain.

## Research funding

**T cell-mediated regulation of mouse neonatal heart regeneration.** American
Heart Association, 2025–2028 ([award 25CDA1454364](https://doi.org/10.58275/AHA.25CDA1454364.pc.gr.229577)).
This project studies how neonatal γδ T cells and IL-17A support heart regeneration
and whether IL-17A can improve repair after the regenerative window closes.

**The role of monocyte infiltration in cardiac regeneration and repair.** American
Heart Association, 2022–2024 ([award 916883](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-6584-0209)).
This project examined whether sustained monocyte recruitment shifts the injured
neonatal heart from regeneration toward fibrotic repair.
